memory_ras.label: ADDDC Sparing (Platform Default)
memory_ras.note: Adaptive Double Device Data Correction (ADDDC) Sparing is the Cisco platform default and VMware recommended RAS mode for enterprise virtualization, providing dynamic DRAM fault tolerance with minimal latency overhead.

memory_ras.label: Hard PPR (Platform Default)
memory_ras.note: Cisco platform default. Hardware fuses out failing DRAM rows across server reboots.

cpu_power.label: C6 State Enabled
cpu_power.note: CPU enters deep C6 sleep during idle, which can introduce microsecond wake latency under bursty vSAN I/O.

cpu_power.label: SpeedStep Enabled
cpu_power.note: CPU frequency scales with load. Disable for consistent low-latency vSAN performance, or ensure vSphere Host Power Policy is High Performance.

cpu_power.label: C1E Enabled
cpu_power.note: Processor lowers frequency and voltage during halt state.

cpu_power.label: Custom Profile
cpu_power.note: Individual BIOS settings govern performance and prefetchers.

cpu_power.label: NUMA Optimized On (Platform Default)
cpu_power.note: Cisco platform default. Exposes native hardware NUMA topology to the hypervisor.

cpu_power.label: Max Performance
cpu_power.note: Processors initialize in maximum performance state during POST and boot.

cpu_power.label: OS Controlled (Platform Default)
cpu_power.note: Cisco platform default. ESXi Host Power Policy governs CPU energy and performance bias.

cpu_power.label: Balanced Performance (Platform Default)
cpu_power.note: Cisco platform default for enterprise virtualization.

cpu_power.label: SNC Disabled
cpu_power.note: Sockets exposed as single NUMA domains — recommended baseline for general virtualization and vSAN.

cpu_power.label: C0/C1 Limit (Platform Default)
cpu_power.note: Cisco platform default. Limits package idle to C0/C1 state for low-latency responsiveness.

cpu_power.label: I/O Sensitive (Platform Default)
cpu_power.note: Cisco platform default. Maximizes I/O and memory throughput across interconnect links.

memory_topology.status_badge: 🔴 Degraded Memory Topology (72% Efficiency)
issues: Asymmetric Socket Memory Allocation: Socket 1 has 48 GB (3 DIMMs) while Socket 2 has 112 GB (7 DIMMs).
Sub-Optimal Memory Interleaving on Socket 1: 3 of 6 channels active (3 DIMMs). Memory bus operating at ~50% bandwidth capacity.
Mixed DIMMs-Per-Channel (DPC) on Socket 2: 7 DIMMs across 6 channels — 1 channel(s) at 2DPC, 5 channel(s) at 1DPC. Non-uniform DPC can reduce memory controller efficiency.
Sub-Optimal Memory Interleaving on Socket 3: 1 of 6 channels active (1 DIMMs). Memory bus operating at ~17% bandwidth capacity.
Sub-Optimal Memory Interleaving on Socket 4: 1 of 6 channels active (1 DIMMs). Memory bus operating at ~17% bandwidth capacity.
recommendations: Re-seat DIMMs so memory capacity and DIMM count are equal between Socket 1 and Socket 2 to avoid asymmetric NUMA node latency.
Install 3 additional DIMM(s) on Socket 1 in empty channels to enable full 6-channel interleaving.
Install DIMMs in multiples of 6 per socket (6 or 12 DIMMs per socket) for uniform 6-channel interleaving.
Install 5 additional DIMM(s) on Socket 3 in empty channels to enable full 6-channel interleaving.
Install 5 additional DIMM(s) on Socket 4 in empty channels to enable full 6-channel interleaving.
